candidates.venue: Lil' Filmmakers Inc.
candidates.description:
“All Below” is a multimedia devised two-person theatre performance that exists in a pocket universe between clown, cosmic horror, and 19th century poetry. Also, there are puppets.
Drawing inspiration from Carlo Rovelli’s book on quantum physics, The Order of Time, as well as the magical realism of Jorge Luis Borges, the performance maroons two Victorian explorers outside of the flow of linear time as their minds attempt to grapple with the impossible and unknowable in their exploration(s) of the phantom island of Saxemberg.

candidates.description: Once dubbed Vietnam’s “Lady Gaga,” Mai Khôi emerged from her life as a pop star to become an internationally lauded human rights activist. Now living in exile in the US, Khôi has created “Bad Activist”: a multimedia autobiography combining original music, projections, and archival footage in a cabaret-style performance that captures her powerful artistry and indomitable spirit. candidates.description:
In a private club, members celebrate the nation's birthday by cosplaying their favorite Americana icons. But the real American myth isn't your Founding Father Fetish. It's the Cowboy. The Capitalist. The Confederate.

One Night Only exists once, lives fully, and then it's gone. You won't find a recording of last night's show. You won't be able to catch the next one and get the same experience. candidates.title: Mischief Night Masters
candidates.venue: Pig Iron Theatre Company
candidates.description:
"I know how men in exile feed on dreams of hope." — Aeschylus
Mischief Night Masters is the RETURN of a once-in-a-generation convergence of Philadelphia’s most exacting and exalted artists. In a night of ecstatic rupture and brutal refinement they summon a force beyond performance—pure invocation. Time folds form breaks the air thickens. What is revealed cannot be unseen. Those permitted to witness will not return the same. Hosted by Betty J. Smithsonian and Sarah Knittel.

candidates.description:
An original solo show about a very unoriginal topic: Dating.
In the absence of a romantic relationship, the next best thing is the attention of a rapt audience. For as long as Tess has been single (forever), the best part of dates has been telling stories about them after. Now she’s ready to share them with everyone else [with names redacted]. Over this 75-minute show, Tess weaves personal storytelling and audience participation about what it means to be 35, ready to mingle, and obsessed with finding meaning in everything. candidates.venue: Skinner Studio / Plays and Players Theatre, 1714 Delancey St
candidates.description: “My Carmillais a queer folk horror theatre piece inspired by J. Sheridan Le Fanu’s 1872 novella, reimagined through a feminist and postcolonial lens. The actors playing Laura and Carmilla will alternate roles each performance, highlighting the question: who is the predator, and who is the prey?Spanning three centuries from colonial New England to the present day, our version of Carmilla uses movement, music, and cast doubling to convey themes of suppression versus freedom.”18+, 5:30pm, $15Featuring:Links:Event page
